build._buildCommand_note: Turbopack (the Next 16 default) was killed on Railway's builder after ~2s: exit 1, no error output, which is a dead process rather than a compile failure. Node's default heap is a fraction of container memory, so it can be OOM-killed while the container still has room; --max-old-space-size raises that ceiling. NOT switching to --webpack: this project's tsconfig maps @/* with no baseUrl, which Turbopack resolves and webpack does not, so that flag trades a memory failure for 20 unresolved-module errors.

deploy._healthcheckPath_note: Served by app/api/health/route.ts. Next binds PORT itself, so there is no port wiring here. Railway routes to whatever the container listens on.
deploy._healthcheckTimeout_note: A Next server boots in seconds, unlike the backend which waits on Postgres and runs migrations first. 60s is generous.
